site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: DRAFT, not approved for real use: needs a clinician's check. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records transcribed from the NCG Guidelines for Urological Malignancies (2019) (National Cancer Grid, India), the prostate cancer pages (investigations p 33, the pathways p 34 to 39, the pathology formats p 53, 54 and 58 to 60), each with its verbatim quote and page. Tiers printed by NCG are kept; the tiers whose tier_basis says 'proposed' or 'proposal' (clinical_history, psa, histopathology, renal_dental_bone_agent) are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). A record NCG gives only under a condition the system never judges (an age, a finding, a plan) is shown with NCG's own tier and the condition, never counted. The book defines low, intermediate and high clinical risk groups by PSA, Gleason score and cT (p 33 and 34); the system never judges the risk group, so a record the book drops for low-risk disease is shown and the board decides. The stage and the risk group are as recorded by the clinician, never computed. Nothing here suggests treatment.
settings_note: Setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes stage or risk group). The four settings follow the book's pathways: localised (T1 to T3a N0, p 34), locally extensive (T3b, or cN1, p 35), metastatic hormone sensitive (p 36) and metastatic castration resistant (p 37 to 39).
